result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.trav_in()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Traverse from selected nodes to inward neighbors. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L6266-L6303){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.trav_in() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} From the currently selected nodes, moves to all nodes that have outward edges leading to the selected nodes (where selected nodes are targets). The current node selection is replaced with the traversed nodes. For directed graphs, follows edges in the reverse direction. For undirected graphs, follows edges in all directions (equivalent to `trav_both()`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} `trav_in()` follows edges in reverse: starting from "C", it lands on "B", the node with an edge pointing into "C": ::: {#e488ed28 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_node("A").add_node("B").add_node("C") graph.add_edge("A", "B") graph.add_edge("B", "C") node_c_id = graph.get_id_from_label("C") graph.select_nodes_by_id([node_c_id]).trav_in() graph.get_selected_node_ids() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [2] ``` ::: :::
